title: CI: FetchContent git clones have no retry backoff, so a brief DNS blip fails the build
description:
### Problem

A momentary DNS failure on a CI runner fails the whole C++ configure step, because CMake's `FetchContent` git-clone retries fire back-to-back with no backoff.

Seen on the macOS 15 x86_64 cache seed ([run 30305581198](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/actions/runs/30305581198)):

```
2026-07-27T21:18:04.4129040Z Cloning into 'zlib-src'...
2026-07-27T21:18:04.4714110Z fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/madler/zlib/': Could not resolve host: github.com
2026-07-27T21:18:04.5721460Z Cloning into 'zlib-src'...
2026-07-27T21:18:04.6439010Z fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/madler/zlib/': Could not resolve host: github.com
2026-07-27T21:18:04.6465780Z Cloning into 'zlib-src'...
2026-07-27T21:18:04.6486180Z fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/madler/zlib/': Could not resolve host: github.com
2026-07-27T21:18:04.6508470Z Had to git clone more than once: 3 times.
CMake Error at zlib-subbuild/zlib-populate-prefix/tmp/zlib-populate-gitclone.cmake:55 (message):
  Failed to clone repository: 'https://github.com/madler/zlib'
```

All three attempts start and fail inside ~236 ms. Three retries against an outage that lasts even a second are three retries against the same failure, so the retry loop buys nothing for exactly the class of fault it exists to absorb.

### Scope

This is not zlib-specific. `src/cpp/ext/CMakeLists.txt` declares 12 dependencies through the same `dependency()` helper, which always uses a git clone:

```cmake
FetchContent_Declare("${_NAME}"
   GIT_REPOSITORY "${${_PREFIX}_REPOSITORY}"
   GIT_TAG        "${${_PREFIX}_REVISION}"
   GIT_SHALLOW    ON
   ...)
```

zlib is simply the first one fetched (`fetch(zlib ZLIB)` at line 421, deliberately ordered ahead of libgit2), so it is the one that reports the failure. Any of the 12 is equally exposed, and any CI job that configures the C++ build can hit this -- PR builds included, not just the cache seeds.

### Notes toward a fix

The retry loop lives in CMake's *generated* `*-gitclone.cmake`, and CMake exposes no knob for the retry count or cadence, so the fix probably has to sit outside it. Some options, none obviously best:

- Retry the cmake configure step at the CI level.
- Cache or pre-warm the `_deps` source trees so a clone isn't needed on every cold build.
- Switch `FetchContent_Declare` to `URL` tarballs with a hash (and possibly a mirror), which downloads through a different code path than `GIT_REPOSITORY`.
- Prefer a system copy where one is reliably available (`RSTUDIO_USE_SYSTEM_<DEP>` already exists as a knob).

### Context

Found while investigating #18373. That issue's underlying cause -- a wrong GWT cache path that made the seed re-run every two hours -- is fixed in #18375; this flake is the unrelated reason that particular run went red, and is filed separately because it affects every platform and every dependency, not just the macOS seed.

title: e2e: Create Playwright E2E workflow for Desktop on MacOS 14 Intel
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Rstudio Desktop open-source needs to be tested on MacOS 14 Intel, for testing during development and for final certification.(Intel).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Create a GitHub Actions workflow that will run the Playwright end-to-end tests for Rstudio Desktop on MacOS 14 Intel. It should be the same as the existing MacOS, Windows, and Ubuntu workflows. It should be possible to 
1) choose between building RStudio from source and using an existing binary
2) run manually, on schedule, or triggered by a PR.
Initially, it should be triggered manually. It can be scheduled and/ordered PR-triggered at a later date.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Relying on operating systems installed on dedicated hardware or in VMs, with the Playwright tests kicked off manually.

**Additional context**
Several similar workflows already exist for MacOS, Windows, and Ubuntu.

title: Shiny-app test should fail fast when the assistant never launches the app, and fix its 300s-poll-vs-120s-timeout mismatch
Readline-notification test should fail fast when the assistant never blocks, not hang to timeout
Plots-pane-activation test should verify a plot was drawn, not trust the assistant's marker
description:
## Summary

`e2e/rstudio/tests/panes/posit-assistant-chat/plots-pane-activation.test.ts` (the #18037 regression test) treats the assistant's `PLOT_DONE_E2E` reply as proof that a plot was drawn. But the prompt *instructs* the model to emit that marker "after the plot has been drawn," and the model emits it even when its `executeCode` tool failed and no plot exists. As a result the test cannot distinguish its two failure modes:

- **plot drawn, but Plots pane not activated** — the real #18037 regression the test targets, vs.
- **no plot drawn at all** — e.g. a broken execution tool.

When the second happens, the test fails at the pane-activation assertion with the message "Plots pane was not activated ... (issue #18037)", which points at the wrong subsystem.

## How it surfaced

Running `@ai` tests against RStudio daily `2026.08.0-daily+139` + Posit Assistant `0.8.9`, this test failed at the activation assertion. The page snapshot showed the `executeCode` tool result was `r.getLogger is not a function` (posit-dev/assistant#1893) — `plot(1:10, ...)` never executed (the console showed only the test's own `graphics.off()` calls), so no plot reached the device. The assistant still replied `PLOT_DONE_E2E` because the prompt told it to. The failure looked like an #18037 regression but was actually the executeCode outage; #18037 itself is not regressed, it just can't be exercised while executeCode is dead.

## Proposed change

Before asserting Plots-pane activation, gate on a real plot actually existing, so a dead execution tool fails with a self-explaining message instead of masquerading as an #18037 regression. `clearPlots` only enables when the Plots pane has history — the same signal the test's `afterAll` already uses, and `isCommandEnabled` is already imported.

Insert between the completion poll (currently ~line 115) and the activation assertion (~line 119):

```ts
// The assistant emits PLOT_DONE_E2E because the prompt tells it to "after
// the plot has been drawn" -- it will say so even if its executeCode tool
// failed and no plot exists. Gate on real plot history (clearPlots only
// enables when the Plots pane has a plot) so a dead executeCode tool fails
// here with a clear message instead of masquerading as an #18037 regression.
await expect
  .poll(() => isCommandEnabled(page, 'clearPlots'), {
    timeout: 15000,
    message:
      'Assistant reported PLOT_DONE_E2E but no plot was drawn -- executeCode ' +
      'likely errored ("r.getLogger is not a function", assistant #1893). ' +
      'Cannot exercise #18037.',
  })
  .toBe(true);
```

## Notes / constraints

- This does not weaken the #18037 assertion — it front-runs it with a clearer precondition, keeping the two failure modes distinct.
- Diagnostic hardening only. It will (correctly) still fail while posit-dev/assistant#1893 is unfixed — it just pins the failure to "no plot drawn" rather than to plot-pane activation.
- Confirm `clearPlots` reliably enables once a plot lands (the poll timeout already absorbs background-render latency).

## Scope

Developer/test-tooling only; no product behavior change, no NEWS.md entry. Suggested branch prefix `test/`. Related: posit-dev/assistant#1893 (root cause of the observed failure); #18037 (the regression this test guards).

Bypass "session-limit" by reopening a project
description: ### System details RStudio Edition : Server RStudio Version : 2026.06.0 OS Version : RedHat Entreprise Linux - 9.6 R Version : 4.4.1 / 4.5.1 /etc/rstudio/profiles [*] max-processes = 800 session-limit=3 ### Steps to reproduce the problem 1. Open the maximum number of sessions from the Workbench; 3 session max, according to our configuration. Note that the button to create a session is disabled. 2. Open a session and scroll through the list of projects. 3. Select a project and the associated action “Open the project in a new R session.” 4. A new session—in this case, a fourth one—is successfully opened and visible in the Workbench. ### Describe the problem in detail You can bypass the maximum session limit configured on the server side by opening projects using the associated button. ### Describe the behavior you expected We would like the behavior to be identical to what occurs when attempting to open an additional session from within an already open session -> An error message - [x] I have read the guide for [submitting good bug reports](https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/wiki/Writing-Good-Bug-Reports). - [ ] I have installed the latest version of RStudio, and confirmed that the issue still persists. - [ ] If I am reporting an RStudio crash, I have included a [diagnostics report](https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us/articles/200321257-Running-a-Diagnostics-Report). - [x] I have done my best to include a minimal, self-contained set of instructions for consistently reproducing the issue.
